title: 2013 HMMT November Guts Problem 10
statement:
How many pairs of real numbers \((x, y)\) satisfy the equation

\[y^{4}-y^{2}=x y^{3}-x y=x^{3} y-x y=x^{4}-x^{2}=0 ?\]

solutions.text: 9 We can see that if they solve the first and fourth equations, they are automatically solutions to the second and third equations. Hence, the solutions are just the \(3^{2}=9\) points where \(x, y\) can be any of \(-1,0,1\).
